lead: A singly reinforced rectangular beam is a concrete beam with steel only on the tension side. At collapse, the concrete in compression carries a resultant force and the steel carries tension. The neutral axis depth xu follows from balancing the concrete compression against the steel tension, together with the moment equation. Strain compatibility fixes the limiting depth xu,max that keeps the section ductile. The two forces are then used to get the moment. This is the standard IS 456 limit state flexure calculation for building beams, footings and many water-retaining members. It is the first flexure design most students meet.
prereq: You need: Unit 1 on stress block parameters, characteristic strength and partial safety factors.

blocks.text: At ultimate limit state, a cracked beam is treated as a concrete compression zone and a steel tension tie. Plane sections remain plane, so strains vary linearly with distance from the neutral axis. Concrete has almost no tensile strength after cracking, so concrete below the neutral axis is ignored. IS 456 replaces the curved concrete stress distribution by an equivalent block. Its resultant compression is C = 0.36 fck b xu, acting at 0.42 xu from the compression face. The steel force is T = 0.87 fy Ast. Here b is width in mm, d is effective depth in mm from the compression face to the tension steel centroid, D is overall depth in mm, xu is neutral axis depth in mm, fck is concrete characteristic cube strength in N/mm², fy is steel yield strength in N/mm², and Ast is tension steel area in mm². The lever arm is z = d − 0.42 xu. Equilibrium C = T gives the steel area once xu is known. The steel is called the tension steel and its area is Ast. When only tension steel is provided, the section is singly reinforced.
C = 0.36 fck b xu    T = 0.87 fy Ast    z = d − 0.42 xu
blocks.where: C is concrete compression in N; T is steel tension in N; fck is in N/mm²; b and xu are in mm; fy is in N/mm²; Ast is in mm²; d and z are in mm.

blocks.text: Mu = 0.36 fck b xu (d − 0.42 xu) = 0.87 fy Ast z
blocks.where: Mu is the factored moment in N·mm; other symbols are as above. Divide by 10⁶ to get kN·m.

blocks.text: To keep the section ductile, xu must not exceed xu,max. IS 456 gives xu,max/d = 0.53 for Fe250, 0.48 for Fe415 and 0.46 for Fe500. The limiting moment is Mu,lim = 0.36 fck b xu,max (d − 0.42 xu,max). If Mu ≤ Mu,lim, the section can be singly reinforced. If Mu > Mu,lim, compression steel is needed; see 2.3. Minimum tension steel is 0.85 b d / fy. Maximum tension steel is 0.04 b D. The minimum prevents sudden brittle failure. The maximum avoids congestion and over-reinforcement. Design aids in 2.5 tabulate the same equation.

items: Fix b, D, d, fck, fy and the factored moment Mu in N·mm.
Find xu,max from xu,max/d: 0.53 for Fe250, 0.48 for Fe415, 0.46 for Fe500.
Compute Mu,lim = 0.36 fck b xu,max (d − 0.42 xu,max).
If Mu ≤ Mu,lim, solve Mu = 0.36 fck b xu (d − 0.42 xu) for the smaller root xu.
Check 0.85 b d / fy ≤ Ast ≤ 0.04 b D; then choose bars and detail.

blocks.text: After Ast is known, choose bars so the provided area is at least the required area. Keep clear cover and bar spacing as required for durability and placing. The chosen bars fix the actual d; if it differs much from the assumed d, repeat the calculation. Check xu/d ≤ xu,max/d. This confirms an under-reinforced section that yields before concrete crushes; the failure modes are compared in 2.2. A beam must also pass serviceability checks for deflection and crack width at service loads; see 2.6. Shear, torsion and bond are checked separately in Unit 3. For a one-way slab the same flexure equation appears in Unit 4, with b taken as 1000 mm.

figure.caption: The flow starts with beam data, finds the limiting moment, and checks whether the section can remain singly reinforced. A failed check sends the design to a doubly reinforced section, not to extra tension steel alone.

spec.aria: Flowchart from beam data to limiting moment, then a check that chooses singly reinforced design or points to doubly reinforced design.

examples.question: Design the tension steel for a singly reinforced rectangular beam: b = 230 mm, overall depth D = 450 mm, effective depth d = 400 mm, fck = 25 N/mm², fy = 415 N/mm², factored moment Mu = 120 kN·m. Check that the section is singly reinforced and give a bar arrangement.
steps: Data: Mu = 120 kN·m = 120 × 10⁶ N·mm; b = 230 mm; d = 400 mm; D = 450 mm; fck = 25 N/mm²; fy = 415 N/mm².
Since 120 kN·m ≤ 126.93 kN·m, the section is singly reinforced.
Solve 120 × 10⁶ = 0.36 × 25 × 230 × xu × (400 − 0.42 xu). This gives 869.4 xu² − 828000 xu + 120 × 10⁶ = 0. The smaller root is xu = 178.31 mm; the other root is greater than d and is not valid.
Check xu/d = 178.31/400 = 0.446 ≤ 0.48, so the section is under-reinforced.
Minimum Ast = 0.85 b d / fy = 0.85 × 230 × 400 / 415 = 188.4 mm². Maximum Ast = 0.04 b D = 0.04 × 230 × 450 = 4140 mm². The value 1022.3 mm² lies between them.
Provide 3 bars of 22 mm: area = 3 × π/4 × 22² = 1140.4 mm², which is greater than 1022.3 mm².
examples.answer: The section is singly reinforced: xu = 178.31 mm and Ast = 1022.3 mm²; provide 3 bars of 22 mm giving 1140.4 mm², with Mu,lim = 126.93 kN·m.
examples.check:
import math
Mu = 120e6
b = 230
d = 400
D = 450
fck = 25
fy = 415
xu_max = 0.48*d
Mu_lim = 0.36*fck*b*xu_max*(d - 0.42*xu_max)
A = 0.36*fck*b*0.42
B = -0.36*fck*b*d
C = Mu
disc = B*B - 4*A*C
xu = (-B - math.sqrt(disc))/(2*A)
z = d - 0.42*xu
Ast = Mu/(0.87*fy*z)
bar_area = 3*math.pi*(22/2)**2
print(f'{Mu_lim/1e6:.2f}')
print(f'{xu:.2f}')
print(f'{Ast:.1f}')
print(f'{bar_area:.1f}')

traps: Using overall depth D in place of effective depth d in the moment equation and in the lever arm. The steel centroid sets d; D is only for the maximum steel check.
Using fy directly in place of 0.87 fy. 0.87 fy is the design strength of the steel. The partial safety factor 1.15 on fy gives 1/1.15 ≈ 0.87, so use 0.87 fy in T and in the moment equation.
Forgetting the xu ≤ xu,max check. Too much tension steel makes an over-reinforced section that crushes before yielding.
Mixing kN·m and N·mm. Use 1 kN·m = 10⁶ N·mm before substituting into any formula.
Taking b as a large flange width for a rectangular beam. Flange width belongs to T and L beams; see 2.4.

quiz.q: Why is concrete below the neutral axis ignored at ultimate limit state?
quiz.a: After cracking, concrete has very little tensile strength, so the tension is carried by steel. The cracked concrete only adds negligible force.

quiz.q: A beam has b = 250 mm, d = 450 mm, fck = 20 N/mm², fy = 500 N/mm² and Mu = 100 kN·m. Is it singly reinforced?
quiz.a: xu,max = 0.46 × 450 = 207 mm. Mu,lim = 0.36 × 20 × 250 × 207 × (450 − 0.42 × 207) = 135.28 kN·m. Since 100 ≤ 135.28, yes, it can be singly reinforced.

quiz.q: For b = 230 mm, d = 400 mm, fck = 25 N/mm², fy = 415 N/mm² and Mu = 120 kN·m, find Ast.
quiz.a: xu,max = 192 mm; Mu,lim = 126.93 kN·m > 120 kN·m. Solving gives xu = 178.31 mm and z = 325.11 mm. Ast = 120 × 10⁶ / (0.87 × 415 × 325.11) = 1022.3 mm².

quiz.q: A beam is detailed with Ast equal to 1.5 times the balanced steel. What happens at ultimate load?
quiz.a: It is over-reinforced. Concrete crushes before the steel yields. Failure is brittle, with little warning deflection. Redesign the section or add compression steel.

quiz.q: Why is xu,max/d smaller for Fe500 than for Fe250?
quiz.a: Higher grade steel needs a larger yield strain. To ensure the steel yields before concrete crushing at ultimate, the neutral axis must be shallower, so xu,max/d is lower.

quiz.q: Why is 0.87 fy used instead of fy for the steel force?
quiz.a: The factor 0.87 is approximately 1/1.15, the partial safety factor for steel. It converts characteristic yield strength to design yield strength.

beyond: Not for the exam. In practice, spreadsheets and BIM tools use the same equilibrium equation but add bar congestion, fire cover and ductile detailing checks. Modern codes keep the same block-and-tie idea; researchers refine concrete confinement and strain limits for high-strength materials. Search for IS 456 flexure, design aids, and ductility of RC beams.
